metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Januar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.94

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Januar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.94
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.94
- Datum: 01.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, As I know you will be anxious about
your child I want to give you some details about her new guardians.
I know Albrecht Schaeffer since twenty years, he is from a very good
protestant family and an excellent poet - all his books have been
published at the Insel - and an upright caracter, our friends the Belau
or Fricental can give you full information. In the last years he did
more philosophe and abstract work, has retired into the country and
his wife, who is a very intelligent, active and motherly person, has always
managed his material life; you may rely upon her, she is not greedy
or business-like and the nation will be an excellent one. I like that
Eva should be in a niet atmosphere of English, American and also
some, but only some Jewish children, get accostumed to an simple
but in the same time intelligent way of life and remain friends of
America in a continental atmosphere. Schaeffers left by disgust and
sentiment of freedom without racial or political reasons, they are
upright people like Haas and Belau without the resentment and
exaltation of the Newyork-refugees. I am sure it will work well and
as I am very sceptical about the manner of pure American education
which is superficial and creates but an arrogant shallowness, I
am glad that she will be in a nation which combines strictness
and order with intelligence and culture. Furthermore we will be
near the next months and so you can be absolutely sure, please do
not worry; we have felt our responsability and closer after con-
sidering all the most various possibilities before (there was an ex-
cellent doctors faculty but it was in Newyork and there she would
have had no company and not the right opportunity of being in
the open air) it is better for the future, not to be educated as a
society-lady but accostumed to practical simple life as you have been
in your birthplace. - We ourselves are anxious to leave Newyork. I
get depressed in being the luxury-shops, the thoughtlessness of all this
people, the stupidity of the refugees and the lack of real compassion

[Randnotiz links:] I hope to go to Newhaven, a little town 112 from Newyork but which contains the
Vale University with the library, there we will live the next two months and work
and study; I had yesterday a long talk with [?]
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Die Randnotiz links ist vertikal geschrieben. Die Randnotiz rechts (auf dem Scan nicht vollständig lesbar, aber im Textfluss erkennbar) wurde in den Haupttext integriert oder als Teil des Randes transkribiert.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur und der Randnotizen. Einige wenige Wörter sind aufgrund der kursiven Handschrift leicht interpretativ, aber im Kontext eindeutig.
